note: Classical Sallusto/Lanzavecchia CD8 memory layout on CCR7 × CD45RA. Strategy: (1) Naive_CD8 anchors on the dense blob at the upper-right corner (CCR7 very high, CD45RA high) — antigen-inexperienced naive cytotoxic T cells. (2) EMRA_CD8 sits immediately to the left of Naive_CD8 in the upper CD45RA band — terminally differentiated cytotoxic T cells. (3) In the lower CD45RA band (memory cells), CCR7 is bimodal — locate the CCR7+ peak; CM_CD8 (central memory; lymph-node homing) sits at/right of this peak, EM_CD8 (effector memory) sits to its left. CCR7 (and sometimes CD45RA) can be trimodal in this panel, so density peaks — not fixed thresholds — anchor the gate.
tips: Classical Sallusto/Lanzavecchia CD8 memory scheme (CCR7 × CD45RA). Naive_CD8: CCR7+ CD45RA+. CM_CD8: CCR7+ CD45RA-. EM_CD8: CCR7- CD45RA-. EMRA_CD8: CCR7- CD45RA+. In-panel co-marker priors (available for QC / downstream refinement, not gated here): (1) CD127 (IL-7Rα) — homeostatic memory marker; Naive/CM tend to be CD127+, EM/EMRA tend toward decreased CD127; useful as an orthogonal memory-axis QC. (2) PD-1 — naïve should be PD-1 negative; PD-1+ within Naive_CD8 flags contamination or TSCM-like events (true TSCM needs CD95, not in panel). (3) HLA-DR and CD25 (in panel, currently unused) mark recent activation and could refine 'activated memory' within CM/EM. Classical refinement markers NOT in panel: CD45RO, CD27, CD28, CD95, CD57, KLRG1.
